dict.string: Touchward reads your calendar only to schedule a nudge when each event ends. Event details are used at that moment on this phone and are never stored, copied, or transmitted by the app.
Touchward reads your calendar only to schedule a nudge when each event ends. Event details are used at that moment on this phone and are never stored, copied, or transmitted by the app.
Expo Dev Launcher uses the local network to discover and connect to development servers running on your computer.

Touchward schedules reminders and calendar nudges on this phone so you remember to tap. Notifications are created locally; nothing about them is stored by the app beyond your settings or sent anywhere.

Touchward requests access to calendar events and notifications solely to provide its features on this device. Calendar data is read at runtime to schedule local notifications and is not retained. The app stores its own settings and the reward counter locally. Four things can leave the device, none with personal identifiers: messages you send through the support form (what you type, plus device model and app version) and, unless turned off in the app, crash reports (the error, app version, device model, OS version, and the app's settings), both to the Touchward support inbox; unless turned off in the app, usage analytics through Google Analytics for Firebase (which features are used, session counts, app version, device model, OS version, language, and country, tied to a random app instance identifier, with no advertising identifier); and, for the optional one time unlock, the App Store purchase receipt and a random app generated identifier to RevenueCat, which confirms and restores the purchase. No name, email, or account exists to link any of it to.

Touchward contains no custom or proprietary encryption. Network requests (the optional support form, push token registration, crash reports, purchases, and usage analytics) use HTTPS through the operating system's standard networking stack, which is exempt encryption under U.S. export rules. ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption is therefore false.
